name: What office construction mistakes are common in first-time tenant improvements?

mainEntity.name: What mistakes do first-time tenants make when planning an office build-out in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: What mistakes do first-time tenants make when planning an office build-out in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: First-time tenants often underestimate how many decisions go into an office build-out. The most common mistakes are signing a lease before understanding the construction cost, assuming permit approval will be quick, changing the layout after pricing, and overlooking building systems like HVAC, electrical, or fire protection. Many tenants also forget about furniture, data cabling, signage, telecom setup, move costs, and contingency. In Los Angeles, those omissions can be expensive because labor, permit, and material costs are high enough that small misses become major budget problems. Another common issue is assuming the landlord allowance will cover everything. It usually does not. The safest path is to get a detailed contractor budget early, confirm the lease approval process, and keep the layout as simple as the business needs allow. Clear scope and realistic timing prevent most first-project mistakes.
acceptedAnswer.description: Common mistakes include signing a lease before pricing the build-out, underestimating permit time, changing the layout too late, and ignoring HVAC or electrical capacity. Tenants also often forget that furniture, data cabling, and move-in costs can be significant. Early budgeting and a detailed scope prevent most surprises.
